faqs.question: What is the Refrigerated/Heated Circulating Bath used for?
faqs.answer: It's a laboratory temperature control platform used for cooling and heating applications from −40°C to +200°C, including precise control near or below ambient temperature.

faqs.question: How precise is the temperature control?
faqs.answer: The bath holds its set point to ±0.005°C, across the full working range, not just near ambient.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right controller type?
faqs.answer: Choose Advanced Programmable (AP) for icon-guided, programmable setup, Advanced Digital (AD) or Standard Digital (SD) for straightforward digital control, or MX or DX Digital depending on your application's specific interface needs; Inkarp confirms the best fit for your workflow.

faqs.question: How do I determine the right reservoir capacity for my application?
faqs.answer: Match the capacity to your sample volume and batch size: 7 liters suits compact bench work, while 28 or 45 liters suits larger-batch or multi-vessel applications; Inkarp can confirm the exact fit based on your working volume.

faqs.question: What is Cool Command technology?
faqs.answer: Cool Command efficiently and quickly extracts heat, even at elevated temperatures, to maintain precise temperature control under load.

faqs.question: Is this bath suitable for flammable liquids?

faqs.question: Does the bath support external circulation?

faqs.question: What accessories are included?

body: Five controller types, five reservoir capacities, and three pump types combine independently, so the bath you order is built around your application, not the other way round.
The range is wide, and the control is tight. −40°C to +200°C is the working span; ±0.005°C is how precisely the bath holds whatever point inside that span you actually need.
Heat comes out fast, even when it's hot. Cool Command extracts heat efficiently at elevated temperatures, which is exactly where precision usually gets hardest to hold.
It's quiet enough to work beside. WhisperCool keeps noise below conversational speech at two meters, while also cutting energy consumption and extending equipment life.
Every unit does more than one job. Internal and external circulation are both standard, so the same bath can condition its own reservoir and feed an external process.
Safety systems don't wait for a problem. Redundant over-temperature protection, high and low limit alarms, and lockout capability catch issues before they become incidents.
Flammable liquid work has its own standard. Advanced Series controllers meet DIN 12876-1 Class III, with temperature and float shut-off systems built for that specific risk.

body: The headline range, −40°C to +200°C, only matters if the bath actually holds where you put it, and that's what the ±0.005°C stability figure is really about.

Getting there depends on two systems working together. WhisperCool manages heat removal quietly and efficiently across normal operation, while Cool Command specifically handles the harder problem: pulling heat out fast when you're running at elevated temperatures, which is exactly when precision usually starts to slip. sections.eyebrow: Controller Tiers: Temperature, Wattage and Stability
sections.title: Matching a controller type to your precision requirement
body: Each controller tier is a genuinely different product, not a rebadged version of the same hardware, and the numbers back that up.

PX reaches the same 200°C ceiling as AP and AD, but does it at 1,200 W with ±0.004°C stability, the tightest in the line. AP matches PX's temperature range at a lower 1,100 W and slightly looser ±0.005°C. AD holds the same range and wattage as AP but loosens to ±0.01°C, the trade-off for digital rather than programmable control. DX caps at 175°C with ±0.01°C stability. SD caps lower still, at 170°C, with ±0.04°C. MX is the most basic tier: 135°C ceiling, ±0.07°C stability, and no 28-liter option at all.
